decisions.reason: Cites profile-introspection.txt Junction/Target and the cordis.patch.yml link marker; states the profile entry is the same directory as the repo, repo edits are the deployment, and Copy-Item was never right for this mode, contrasted with a copied dependency.

Grounds both locks in the running dsh host: the host serves client.js and holds lib/index.js open, so closing the browser tab releases nothing; separately explains browser caching of the served bundle requiring cache-bypassing refresh after host restart, without calling caching a filesystem lock or generalizing to all DSH versions.

Explains both paths are the same physical directory via the junction, so renaming renamed the source files and the follow-up copy found no source. Recovery: stop host (precaution), rename client.js.old2/index.js.old2 back preserving contents, verify with node --check on both, then activate; does not require renaming while locked or recreating files.

Gives the correct dependency order: fully stop the host process (not the browser), restart dsh web, hard-refresh with cache bypass because the browser may still serve cached client.js, then verify the feature marker, route behavior, and absence of load errors; states restart of the browser alone is insufficient.

Presents a pre-flight Get-Item LinkType/Target check plus the cordis.patch.yml link: marker before any file operation, distinguishes linked from copied installs, and explains why copy-into-node_modules advice is actively harmful for link installs (copies repo onto itself; EBUSY workarounds mutate the source).

caps.reason: All copying advice is quoted only as the rejected mistake; the final recovery explicitly renames .old2 back, forbids any copy step, and treats both paths as one directory.
The report explicitly rejects browser refresh/tab close as sufficient and its final plan requires stopping and restarting the dsh host process before hard-refresh and verification.
